nodes.content: Identify causally responsible actions in partially observed reinforcement learning despite delayed rewards and correlated, reward-irrelevant actions.
requirements: Define counterfactual action contributions and establish their identifiability limits under hidden confounding.
Reach matched returns using 30% fewer environment interactions than recurrent PPO on delayed-reward tasks.

nodes.content: Develop CounterTrace: randomized probes estimate history-conditioned delayed-return contrasts, sensitivity bounds quantify hidden confounding, and contrast-weighted advantages train recurrent PPO.
Can sparse randomized probes identify delayed-return action contributions, and what can be bounded in unprobed histories with hidden confounding?
CounterTrace identifies probed-history contrasts; unprobed histories require observational overlap, with Γ≤2 sensitivity bounds excluding zero for ≥80% high-impact actions.
Randomize 5% of actions; test overlap, estimate delayed-return contrasts, derive Γ≤2 sensitivity bounds, benchmark CounterTrace against recurrent PPO.
Run 20-seed ProbeMaze-Delayed with 5% probes; compare oracle contrasts and Γ≤2 bound coverage across hidden-confounding strata.
ProbeMaze-Delayed: probed contrasts had 0.06 MAE; Γ≤2 bounds covered 94% of oracle effects, excluding zero for 83% high-impact actions.
Retain 5% randomized probes and Γ≤2 bounds for attribution; 0.06 MAE and 94% coverage justify sample-efficiency testing.
With retained 5% probes and Γ≤2 bounds, compare CounterTrace against recurrent PPO on interactions-to-matched-return across delayed tasks, targeting ≥30% savings.
Benchmark CounterTrace against recurrent PPO over 20 seeds on ProbeMaze-Delayed, KeyDoor-Delay, and DistractorChain; record interactions to 80%-oracle return.
CounterTrace Benchmark v1: 20-seed learning curves and paired-bootstrap intervals for interactions to 80%-oracle return across three delayed tasks.
Audit CounterTrace Benchmark v1 curves and confidence intervals; calculate per-task interaction savings versus recurrent PPO and test the 30% target.
CounterTrace reached 80%-oracle return with 36% fewer interactions than recurrent PPO across three tasks (20 seeds; 95% CI: 31–41%).
Does CounterTrace avoid attributing delayed rewards to correlated distractor actions that have no causal effect on return?
Inject reward-correlated, causally inert toggle actions into DistractorChain; measure false-attribution rate against oracle interventions over 20 seeds.
On DistractorChain, CounterTrace labeled 38% of inert toggles high-impact (|contrast|≥0.1 return units), versus 0% by oracle intervention.
Develop SwitchPair: stratified randomized action swaps identify probed effects; inert-toggle controls and Γ-bounded credit gate policy updates elsewhere.
Can SwitchPair suppress false credit for inert toggles while retaining 30% interaction savings with a 5% swap budget?
At 5% swaps, SwitchPair cuts inert-toggle false-attribution below 10% and reaches 80%-oracle return using ≥30% fewer interactions than recurrent PPO.
Using Benchmark v1 baselines, run 20-seed SwitchPair with 5% swaps across three tasks; measure inert-toggle misattribution and interaction savings.
SwitchPair cut DistractorChain inert-toggle false-attribution from 38% to 7%, but saved only 22% interactions versus recurrent PPO.
Retain SwitchPair’s inert-toggle controls, but revise swap allocation: false-attribution fell from 38% to 7%, while savings missed 30%.
Uncertainty-weighted 5% swaps, calibrated against inert-toggle controls, retain ≤10% false-attribution and restore ≥30% interaction savings.
Run 20-seed, 5%-swap uncertainty-weighted versus uniform SwitchPair trials across three tasks; measure inert-toggle false-attribution and recurrent-PPO-relative interaction savings.
Uncertainty-weighted SwitchPair achieved 8% inert-toggle false-attribution and 33% fewer interactions than recurrent PPO across three tasks (20 seeds).
Formalize swap identification and hidden-confounding bounds; verify uncertainty-weighted SwitchPair’s ≥30% savings and ≤10% inert-toggle misattribution on held-out tasks.
Derive identification of history-conditioned swap contrasts under randomization and positivity; construct observationally equivalent hidden-confounder models and Γ≤2 bounds.
SwitchPair Theorem v1 defines counterfactual return contrasts, proves randomized-swap identification under overlap, and supplies hidden-confounding counterexamples and Γ≤2 bounds.
Develop DelayKnockoff: conditional-history knockoffs filter correlated distractors, randomized audits identify action contrasts, and sensitivity-gated advantages train recurrent PPO.
Derive randomized-audit identification and confounding bounds; test DelayKnockoff’s ≥30% interaction savings and ≤10% inert-toggle false-attribution on held-out tasks.
Using Benchmark v1’s metrics, run 20-seed DelayKnockoff versus recurrent-PPO trials on held-out DelayVault; measure misattribution and interactions-to-80%-oracle.
DelayVault Benchmark v1 contains 20-seed learning curves, inert-toggle attribution labels, and interactions-to-80%-oracle comparisons with recurrent PPO.
Audit DelayVault Benchmark v1’s interaction savings and false-attribution; check SwitchPair Theorem v1’s Γ≤2 bounds against oracle effects.
On DelayVault, DelayKnockoff saved 34% interactions versus recurrent PPO, misattributed 6% inert toggles; Γ≤2 bounds covered 93% oracle effects.
Advance DelayKnockoff and SwitchPair to cross-task validation: both exceeded 30% interaction savings with ≤8% inert-toggle misattribution.
DelayVault Audit Report v1 provides verified learning curves, inert-toggle confusion counts, and Γ≤2 bound-coverage checks for cross-task validation.
Using DelayVault Audit Report v1 to freeze calibration, cross-evaluate SwitchPair and DelayKnockoff on EchoMaze-Delay: savings, misattribution, Γ≤2 coverage.
EchoMaze-Delay: SwitchPair saved 18% interactions versus recurrent PPO, misattributing 16% inert toggles; DelayKnockoff saved 32%, misattributing 7%.
Does DelayKnockoff’s 7% EchoMaze misattribution persist when hidden-state shifts break conditional-history knockoff exchangeability?
Using DelayVault Audit Report v1, shift hidden-state mixtures within identical histories; compare DelayKnockoff misattribution and savings against DelayVault Benchmark v1.
Shifted DelayVault raised DelayKnockoff inert-toggle misattribution from 6% to 24% and cut recurrent-PPO-relative interaction savings from 34% to 19%.
Defer DelayKnockoff deployment pending hidden-state-shift safeguards: unshifted tasks saved 32–34% interactions, but shifted DelayVault misattributed 24% inert toggles.
Build probe-calibrated shift alarms and audit-gated knockoff credit; retest shifted DelayVault for ≤10% misattribution and ≥30% interaction savings.
Calibrate probe-drift alarms against DelayVault Benchmark v1 and 24% shift failure; rerun 20-seed shifted gated-credit trials, measuring misattribution and savings.
DelayVault Benchmark v2 extends v1 with probe-drift alarms, shifted-mixture gated-credit learning curves, inert-toggle misattribution, and recurrent-PPO interaction comparisons.
Develop SentinelCredit: randomized probes identify action contrasts; shift-robust sensitivity bounds suppress unsupported distractor credit and gate recurrent-PPO advantages.
Can SentinelCredit keep inert-toggle misattribution below 10% under hidden-state shifts while preserving 30% interaction savings?
With 5% probes and Γ≤2 credit gating, SentinelCredit yields ≤10% inert-toggle misattribution and ≥30% interaction savings on shifted DelayVault.
Using DelayVault Benchmark v2, run 20-seed shifted SentinelCredit trials with 5% probes and Γ≤2 gates; measure misattribution and recurrent-PPO-relative savings.
Shifted DelayVault: SentinelCredit misattributed 8% inert toggles and saved 31% interactions versus recurrent PPO across 20 seeds.
Formalize SentinelCredit’s probe-identified contrasts and hidden-confounding limits; replicate ≥30% savings and ≤10% misattribution on shifted EchoMaze-Delay.
Transfer DelayVault Benchmark v2 alarm thresholds to shifted EchoMaze-Delay; run 20-seed SentinelCredit trials measuring interaction savings and inert-toggle misattribution.
Shifted EchoMaze Replication v1 records 20-seed SentinelCredit learning curves, inert-toggle labels, frozen alarm thresholds, and recurrent-PPO interaction baselines.
Audit Shifted EchoMaze Replication v1: compute paired-bootstrap interaction savings, inert-toggle misattribution, and probe-contrast coverage against oracle interventions.
Shifted EchoMaze-Delay: SentinelCredit saved 32% interactions versus recurrent PPO, misattributed 9% inert toggles; Γ≤2 bounds covered 94% oracle contrasts.
Develop LatentBridge: estimate proximal action contrasts using negative-control proxies and randomized probes, then train recurrent PPO on uncertainty-gated advantages.
When do negative-control proxies identify unprobed action contrasts under hidden confounding, and can LatentBridge retain ≥30% interaction savings?
Under proxy exclusion, completeness, and overlap, LatentBridge identifies unprobed contrasts and saves ≥30% interactions versus recurrent PPO.
Using Shifted EchoMaze Replication v1, simulate valid negative-control proxies; test overlap, bridge rank, oracle-contrast error, and recurrent-PPO-relative interaction savings.
With valid, full-rank EchoMaze proxies, LatentBridge achieved 0.05 oracle-contrast MAE but saved only 24% interactions versus recurrent PPO.
With valid, full-rank proxies, uncertainty-targeted probes preserve ≤0.06 oracle-contrast MAE and raise LatentBridge’s interaction savings from 24% to ≥30%.
Using Shifted EchoMaze Replication v1, run 20-seed LatentBridge with 5% uncertainty-targeted probes; measure oracle-contrast MAE and recurrent-PPO-relative interaction savings.
Uncertainty-targeted LatentBridge achieved 0.05 oracle-contrast MAE and 31% fewer interactions than recurrent PPO on shifted EchoMaze (20 seeds).
Prioritize SentinelCredit’s 32% savings; conditionally advance LatentBridge’s 31% with validated proxies, avoiding DelayKnockoff’s shift failure and untargeted 24%.
Define SentinelCredit’s counterfactual contrasts and hidden-confounding bounds; validate LatentBridge proxies; replicate ≥30% savings and ≤10% misattribution on shifted tasks.
Using Shifted EchoMaze Replication v1 and LatentBridge’s 0.05-MAE benchmark, derive SentinelCredit contrasts and test proxy rank and Γ≤2 coverage.

SentinelCredit Theory v1 defines policy-following contrasts, proves randomized-probe identification under overlap, and documents hidden-confounding counterexamples, proxy-rank diagnostics, and Γ≤2 bounds.
On held-out shifted KeyDoor-Delay, test SentinelCredit Theory v1’s Γ≤2 bound coverage and proxy-rank diagnostics; benchmark LatentBridge’s savings and misattribution.
Shifted KeyDoor-Delay: full-rank proxies yielded LatentBridge 31% interaction savings and 8% inert-toggle misattribution; SentinelCredit Γ≤2 bounds covered 93% oracle contrasts.
Keep SentinelCredit primary; advance LatentBridge only with full-rank proxies, given shifted KeyDoor’s 31% savings and 8% misattribution.
